staged_5m_execution_parquet.holdout_boundary_enforcement: Parquet scan enforces item_id IN (74 Phase-One selected_ids) AND ts >= 1759622400 AND ts < 1785024000 AND ts < 1785024300 via DuckDB pushdown BEFORE Python materialization; evaluation windows further enforce available_at < window_end <= 1785024000 < 1785024300. Zero rows at or after 1785024000 / 1785024300 are ever read.
staged_5m_execution_parquet.schema:
item_id: int64
name: string
ts: int64
avg_high_price: double
avg_low_price: double
high_price_volume: int64
low_price_volume: int64
mid_price: double
total_volume: int64

explicit_methodological_limitations.retrospective_not_prospective: P1b is a retrospective execution-resolution experiment on historical development folds (2025-10-29..2026-07-26), holding the hourly signal origins and frozen recursive_student_t quantiles fixed while resolving order execution on historical 300s bars rather than 3600s bars. It is not a live prospective forward test.
explicit_methodological_limitations.five_minute_averaged_quotes_limitation: prices_5m_p1b.parquet is derived from kaggle-5m canonical 300s buckets (volume-weighted 5-minute directional trade averages). Averaged 300s bars CANNOT represent intra-bar limit-order book depth, resting queue priority, hidden liquidity, or continuous-time price paths within a 5-minute interval.
explicit_methodological_limitations.missing_side_and_null_midpoint_handling: mid_price is NULL whenever only one directional side printed in a 300s bar. Missing sides and mid_price are NEVER imputed: directional ask (avg_high_price) and bid (avg_low_price) are tracked independently via causal last-print freshness (high_freshness_seconds, low_freshness_seconds) identically to P1, while per-bucket fill capacity uses observed directional volume (0 when a side did not print, guaranteeing zero fills on non-printing sides).

unchanged_from_p1: Identical 74 items and identical 3 inner-training (21d) + outer-validation (90d) windows (2025-10-29..2026-07-26)
Identical frozen recursive_student_t 768-path quantiles and identical hourly signal timestamps (now = t_hour + 3900), scores, and dynamic allocation_bps
Identical osrs_ml.costs (2.00% GE tax, 49 GP exemption, 5M/unit cap, integer_lots_v2), osrs_ml.execution, and osrs_ml.backtest.simulate machinery

Identical primary ExecutionAssumptions parameters (passive_prices=false, fill_model=bucket_proxy_v1, price_model=integer_lots_v2, participation_bps=200, slippage_bps=10, latency_seconds=300, max_freshness_seconds=7500, buy_timeout_seconds=7500, terminal_haircut_bps=100)
Identical 2x3 training-only tuning grid (H in {4, 24} hours x min_net_edge_bps in {0, 25, 50}) and identical 3 null controls (null_time_shuffled x5, null_sign_flipped, null_detrended_zero_drift)

effective_observation_to_first_eligible_.p1_3600s: Signal submitted at t_hour + 3900; bucket h=1 [t_hour+3600, t_hour+7200) is ineligible because start < submitted + 300; earliest fill bucket is h=2 [t_hour+7200, t_hour+10800) publishing at t_hour + 11100 (3,300s to 7,200s after submission; ~4,200s+ post-origin-end).
effective_observation_to_first_eligible_.p1b_300s_primary_delay300s: Each 300s bucket [ts, ts+300) becomes available at ts + 600 (300s bucket + 300s publication delay, matching hourly.parquet). Signal submitted at t_hour + 3900 (coinciding with bar ts = t_hour + 3300); earliest post-latency fill bar is ts = t_hour + 4200 [t_hour+4200, t_hour+4500) available at t_hour + 4800 (300s to 900s post-submission), with up to 22 post-latency 300s buckets inside buy_timeout_seconds = 7500.
effective_observation_to_first_eligible_.p1b_300s_sensitivity_delay0s: Secondary timing sensitivity with available_at = ts + 300 (0s publication delay on 300s bars; earliest fill bar still ts = t_hour + 4200 available at t_hour + 4500 = 300s to 600s post-submission) plus tight 30-minute buy_timeout_seconds = 1800 sensitivity.

predictions_if_latency_is_binding_constr: P_fill: Unit fill rate on walk-forward (and H24h_edge0bps) increases materially above P1's 6.72% (and 8.91%), specifically >= 15.0% (>2x P1).
P_expiry: Zero-fill buy ceiling-expiry rate shrinks materially below P1's 79.12% (and 75.38%), specifically <= 50.0%.

P_spread: Median realised round-trip spread + slippage compresses materially from P1's 2.64% toward the origin-modelled ~0.79%-0.99% (specifically < 2.00%, cutting the +1.65 to +1.85 pp adverse spread delta by at least one-third).
P_pnl: Walk-forward net P/L moves upward from -71,792 GP into positive territory (> 0 GP), and if latency alone prevented monetisation, clears 168h block-bootstrap p < 0.05 against 0 GP.

falsification_interpretation_rules.case_1_latency_confirmed_and_monetisable: P_fill, P_expiry, P_spread hold AND net P/L > 0 with 168h block-bootstrap p < 0.05 -> 3600s whole-bucket latency was the binding barrier; 300s execution unlocks statistically significant net GP on averaged bars (still subject to live order-book queue validation).
falsification_interpretation_rules.case_2_latency_improves_fills_but_spread: P_fill and P_expiry hold (higher fill rate, lower ceiling-expiry loss), yet realised round-trip spread + 2% GE tax still leaves net P/L <= 0 GP or statistically indistinguishable from 0 GP (p >= 0.05) -> Whole-bucket latency was real for fill mechanics, NOT sufficient for profitability: the Grand Exchange bid-ask spread + 2% tax wall itself dominates recursive_student_t's 1h-24h signal amplitude.
falsification_interpretation_rules.case_3_300s_spread_wider_than_hourly_vwa: Realised round-trip spread on 300s bars does not compress toward 0.99% (or widens above 2.64%) -> Hourly VWAP aggregation smoothed intra-hour bid-ask bounce; true 5-minute directional execution faces an even steeper microstructural spread wall.
